root_cause.text: The `virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb()` function relied on `iter->count` to determine the size for RLIMIT_MEMLOCK accounting via `msg_zerocopy_realloc()`, but this iterator was already consumed by `virtio_transport_fill_skb()` before the function was called, causing `iter->count` to be 0 on the last skb and bypassing memory lock limit enforcement.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly documents that "this function is called after virtio_transport_fill_skb() has already consumed the iterator via __zerocopy_sg_from_iter(), so on the last skb, iter->count will be 0, skipping the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK enforcement." The fix passes `pkt_len` as an explicit parameter instead of reading the already-consumed `iter->count`, matching the approach used by TCP and UDP implementations for proper pinned-pages accounting.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in the `virtio_transport_init_zcopy_skb()` function introduced in this commit. At lines 48-57, the function calls `msg_zerocopy_realloc(sk_vsock(vsk), iter->count, NULL)` where `iter` is `&msg->msg_iter`. However, this iterator has already been consumed by the preceding `virtio_transport_fill_skb()` call (lines 43-47) which invokes `__zerocopy_sg_from_iter(info->msg, NULL, skb, &info->msg->msg_iter, len)`. This means `iter->count` will be 0 or significantly reduced on the last skb iteration, causing `msg_zerocopy_realloc()` to allocate insufficient memory for RLIMIT_MEMLOCK accounting. The code does not save the original iterator count before consuming it, nor does it pass the correct payload length to `msg_zerocopy_realloc()`. The fix would require passing the actual `len` parameter (payload_len) instead of relying on the already-consumed `iter->count`.
